clue.text: Such an affair, if it got about, could become exceptionally bellicose

indicators.note: getting about suggests moving around, so the letters of the phrase are shuffled into a new order

parts.note: exceptionally means extra, as in extra large
bellicose means warlike, martial

explanation.surface: A warning that some liaison, once gossip spreads, could turn very nasty indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: Exceptionally bellicose is EXTRA MARTIAL; 'if it got about' tells you to rearrange those letters, and two of them swap to give the answer. 'could become' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair outside a marriage is described by this adjective, meaning beyond the wedding vows.

clue.text: Apprentice wearing coarse material

indicators.note: the apprentice has the coarse word on, as if wearing it, so it sits inside

parts.note: earthy means crude or coarse
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A trainee is dressed in rough cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like cloth, but is the adjective meaning worldly, not spiritual.
explanation.definitionFit: Material things are worldly, belonging to this world rather than heaven.

clue.text: Pet standing up — it wants to be understood

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up means read upwards, reversing the word

parts.note: a cat is a typical pet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog begging on hind legs wants its master to understand it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' in a down clue reads CAT from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is implied without being spoken, simply understood.

clue.text: Fruit turnover readily available from this carrier

definitions.text: Fruit turnover readily available from this carrier

parts.words: Fruit turnover readily available from this carrier
parts.note: a cart of fruit that is easily tipped over, as in the idiom for spoiling a plan; 'turnover' also suggests a pastry

explanation.definitionFit: This is a barrow loaded with fruit, famously easy to upset in the idiom about ruining a plan.

clue.text: Very dry individual in a way

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road
I is one, a single individual

explanation.surface: A certain person in the street has a very dry wit.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert land with almost no rainfall is parched, the meaning of very dry.

clue.text: The key to starting revolutions

parts.note: read as politics it means the spark of uprising; read mechanically it is the car key turned to make an engine turn over

explanation.definitionFit: A car's starting system is switched on by a key, which gets the engine revolving.

clue.text: A non-drinker in charge in a high position

parts.note: taken as written
TT is teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: A sober person is put in a lofty post of command.
explanation.walkthrough: TT stands for teetotal, a non-drinker; 'in a' joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The room right under the roof is the highest part of a house.

clue.text: Jacobson in a predicament in African republic

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Benin is a republic in West Africa
a jam is a tight spot, a predicament

explanation.surface: A man named Jacobson is in trouble in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jacobson' looks like a surname, but read as Jacob's son: the youngest son of Jacob in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible this was the youngest of Jacob's twelve sons.

clue.text: Did he notice the finches in Australia?

definitions.meaning: the naturalist whose study of Galapagos finches fed his theory of evolution
the capital city of the Northern Territory

explanation.definitionFit: Charles the naturalist studied finches, and the Northern Territory's capital bears his name.

clue.text: Quality of the loud-speaker in the foyer

definitions.meaning: how well a radio set picks up and plays a broadcast signal
the front desk area where hotel guests are greeted

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the clarity of a broadcast signal and the welcome area of a building such as a hotel.

clue.text: Character-building in the Army

parts.note: taken as written
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Military service is said to build a young person's character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' here is a letter of an alphabet, not personality; 'building in' only links. TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character in printing.

clue.text: The art, when concealed, of the tile-maker

indicators.note: the words are disguised, their letters hidden in a rearranged form

explanation.surface: A tiler guards the secret craft of his trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tile' is old British slang for a hat, so a tile-maker is a milliner of men's hats; 'when concealed' disguises THE ART by rearranging it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tile is slang for a hat, and someone who makes hats follows this trade.

clue.text: Cloggy sort of pudding excites Jack's wit

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: A heavy, sticky dessert gets a sailor joking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excites' stirs up the letters of JACK'S WIT; the possessive apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a toffee or pudding so chewy it glues the jaws together, which is why it is called cloggy.

clue.text: Powerful sort of service from one not quite a gentleman

definitions.meaning: the idiom for sterling, valuable help given in time of need
a freeholding farmer ranking just below the gentry in old English society

explanation.definitionFit: Yeoman service is an idiom for loyal, strong help, and a yeoman was a small landowner ranked just below a gentleman.

clue.text: Start shooting 'The Gaping Inferno'

parts.note: gaping means wide open
an inferno is a great fire

explanation.surface: A film called The Gaping Inferno starts its shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start shooting' reads as filming beginning; it means begin firing guns.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin firing weapons at a target is the military order for starting shooting.

clue.text: Poet cut by Oriental medico

indicators.note: the poet's name is split open and another piece sits inside it

parts.note: A. E. Housman, author of A Shropshire Lad
E for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: A poet is attacked by an Eastern doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Housman, the English poet, is the piece split open; E, short for East, sits in the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior hospital doctor in Britain is given this title, and medico is slang for a doctor.

clue.text: They are often fired, which may be why we are short-handed

definitions.meaning: pistols and rifles, weapons discharged by hand

definitions.text: which may be why we are short-handed
definitions.meaning: a joke reading: if our limbs were little we would be short of hands

explanation.definitionFit: Pistols and rifles are handheld guns, and read literally the phrase means little limbs.

clue.text: Brave Napoleonic music espoused by the hard left

indicators.note: to be espoused is to be married, held close, so one piece is embraced by the other

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
Beethoven's Eroica symphony was first dedicated to Napoleon

explanation.surface: Militant leftists adopt a stirring piece of music about Napoleon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the hard left' sounds political, but is H and L around EROICA, Beethoven's Third Symphony; 'the' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: An old form of heroic, meaning courageous and bold.

clue.text: Born nurse comprehends the lung

indicators.note: to comprehend is to include or take in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to rear a child is to nurse and bring it up
taken as written

explanation.surface: A natural carer understands how a patient's lungs work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Born nurse' looks like a phrase about a talented carer; it is B then REAR, which 'comprehends' THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lung is an organ that breathes, so it can playfully be called one that takes air in.

clue.text: Little Boy Blue, for example, and the black cow

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as in pencil grades
a cow lows, so it can be called a lower

explanation.surface: A nursery rhyme with Little Boy Blue and a dark cow in the meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme Little Boy Blue is told to come blow his horn; 'lower' here is one that lows (moos), not something underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Boy Blue is told to blow his horn, so he is someone who blows.

clue.text: Fleshy animal

definitions.meaning: relating to the body and its appetites
physical and bodily rather than spiritual, as in animal urges

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes bodily appetites and desires, which can be called both fleshly and animal.

clue.text: Running, say, on side to be effective

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
a thing that works is effective

explanation.surface: A sports coach claims running on one side is effective.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the half of the field behind the batsman's legs is the on side, also called the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwork such as running about to gather information is tiring practical effort done on foot.

clue.text: Source of screech owl's cry on high branch

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: meat that is high has gone bad, or off

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: an owl's call is a hoot

explanation.surface: A screech owl calls from up in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on high' looks like a location, but 'high' means gone bad, as meat does; 'on' in an across clue puts the later pieces after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoot growing off a main stem is a side branch, and the word also means anything that grows out of something larger.

clue.text: Hotel, unfinished monster, came to nothing

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter, left incomplete

parts.note: the Hydra was a many-headed monster of Greek myth
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A half-built monster of a hotel project came to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the last letter of HYDRA; 'came to' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa hotel offering water cures was given this name in Victorian Britain.

clue.text: Moving quickly, cast set about "The Last of Mrs Cheyney'"

indicators.note: one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to fling is to cast or throw

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A theatre company is rehearsing the play The Last of Mrs Cheyney.
explanation.walkthrough: The Last of Mrs Cheyney is a 1925 play, so the surface is about staging it; but 'set about' puts FLING around Y, the last letter of Cheyney.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going at speed, like a rapid visit, is said to be going at great pace.

clue.text: Soldier set up card game in blockhouse

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means placed upwards, reversed

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
loo is an old card game

explanation.surface: Soldiers set up a card game in a fortified bunker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blockhouse' reads as a fort, but means a house made of blocks of snow; loo is also an old British card game.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit dome is literally a house built of snow blocks.

clue.text: Characterless girl is out of love

indicators.note: one piece lies outside the other, around it

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A dull girl has fallen out of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out of' places ANN around O.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for anonymous, describing something without a name or identity.

clue.text: The Red Queen took precedence, but slipped up

indicators.note: one piece going first means it is placed before the other

parts.note: ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina
taken as written

explanation.surface: In Alice, the Red Queen pushes ahead of others but makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Red Queen' recalls Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass; read as RED and Queen (ER), with the Queen going first.
explanation.definitionFit: To have made a mistake is to have gone wrong, a simple synonym.

clue.text: Funny cartoon about the lieutenant's low woman

indicators.note: one set of letters goes around the other
funny suggests odd or peculiar, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: LT is the usual abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A comic drawing mocks an officer's disreputable girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low woman' sounds disreputable but means a female singer with a deep voice; 'Funny' jumbles the cartoon's letters to CONTRAO before 'about' wraps them round the officer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the lowest female singing voice, so a singer with it is a woman whose range is low.

clue.text: The coaches are going round the reservoir

parts.note: rolling means turning over and over
a stock is a reserve supply held in readiness

explanation.surface: Buses are driving around a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The coaches' suggests buses, but means railway carriages and wagons.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway carriages and wagons are collectively called by this name, coaches being passenger carriages.
